evidence_class: Mocked: fakeredis journal and execution registry, a fake lease clock and an in process API server that applies a create, drops its response and then answers AlreadyExists; no Kubernetes API server, node autoscaler or EC2 call was made.
interfaces: scripts.swarm_v2.kubernetes.client: KubeHttp(server, token_path, context, opener) and KubeHttp.in_cluster(environ, account) send JSON to the API server with the service account token read per request; an unreachable server, an unreadable token and an unreadable answer raise ConnectionError, a read timeout raises TimeoutError

PodClient(http, namespace): create_pod, read_pod (None on 404), list_pods(selector) without a resourceVersion, so a quorum read; 409 AlreadyExists raises AlreadyExists, 429 and 5xx raise ConnectionError, other refusals raise ApiRefused(status, reason)

scripts.swarm_v2.kubernetes.runtime: KubernetesTransport(api, slug, template, creation_enabled) is the OperationTransport for backend kubernetes and action spawn; apply_operation renders the admitted launch with the SV2-KUB-01 PodTemplate, refuses a render whose owner label is not owner_for(slug), whose execution or generation labels disagree with the operation, or whose namespace is not the client namespace, annotates the Pod with its spec digest and operation payload digest, and creates it under the deterministic name swarm-<execution_id>; the applied result carries the Pod uid, name and namespace

On AlreadyExists the transport reads the Pod and adopts it only when owner, execution and generation labels, both digests and the guarded live spec fields (service account, token automount, host namespaces, runtime class, Pod and container security context, image, container count, host path volumes) match the render; otherwise the Pod is quarantined in KubernetesTransport.quarantined with its reason (owner, execution, generation, operation, spec or ambiguous) and the operation is refused; a quarantined Pod is never adopted, patched or deleted

observe_operation lists Pods by the controller-owner and execution-id labels, so Operations.recover in a restarted controller finds the Pod and its uid; an empty list after an unanswered create stays unknown, because a reaped Pod leaves no trace; a second labelled Pod for one execution quarantines both as ambiguous

status(execution_id) returns every labelled Pod of the execution as PodStatus with the Pod phase, status and container termination or waiting reasons and the deleting flag, kept apart from task state; a Succeeded Pod never marks the ledger outcome committed
kubernetes_create_reconciliation_total() counts events per call: created, adopted, observed, quarantined and disabled

supported_versions.kubernetes: core v1 Pod REST calls: label selector list, named read and create answering 409 AlreadyExists; exercised only against the in process fake, no live release
supported_versions.redis: the runtime operation journal and execution registry from SV2-RUN-04 and SV2-CTL-01
supported_versions.compatibility: The local runtime and its transports are unchanged; the transport registers only under backend kubernetes, so a controller without it settles kubernetes operations as unknown, as before

authority: The owner label value comes from owner_for(slug), never from a display label or Pod name. Creation runs only through the controller's fenced transport, which calls the controller's authorization callback and lease check before every apply. Case B revokes the grant callback and the next spawn is refused with no create call; case C shows a stale controller refused after takeover. The callback itself validates nothing in these fixtures.

states.observed: Cases A, B and C each passed twice with identical records in proofs run 38066003376 at tested_commit; that run passed the other 86 client and runtime tests and failed only the three evidence comparisons before these records were committed.
states.accepted: A lost create response followed by observation adopts the original Pod uid; the journal path made one create call and a direct retry reaching AlreadyExists adopted the same uid with a second, refused, create call. A squatting Pod with another execution label is quarantined on each attempt and left unchanged. A restarted controller recovers the uid through the label qualified list, matches it in reconcile and re-issues the spawn from the admission intent without a create. A Pod reaped after a lost response leaves the retry unknown with no second create.
states.committed: Code and fixture inputs are at tested_commit; manifest.json hashes them.
states.externally_verified: None: no live API server or G3 deployment was exercised.

rollback_rehearsal.action: Construct the transport with creation_enabled False: no create call is made while observation, status and the controller's reconcile continue.
rollback_rehearsal.authoritative_objects: The runtime operation journal, the execution registry and the execution Pods themselves; the in memory quarantine list and reconciliation counts are observational.
rollback_rehearsal.proof: Case C takes over with creation disabled: a new launch settles accepted with no create call and the existing Pod is still listed by uid.

remaining_limitations: Observation has no payload, so a Pod found by observation is matched on labels and the operation digest annotation only, without the guarded spec comparison; Pod creation rights in the swarm namespace (SV2-SEC-01) are the boundary there.
A matching Pod that is terminating still settles the spawn applied; its deleting flag shows in status and reconcile counts it as terminating.
An unanswered create whose Pod is gone stays unknown; resolving it needs a new execution generation from the controller.

The execution registry requires a Pod name in the runtime target before admission allocates the execution id, so the target carries a placeholder; the real Pod name and uid live in the operation journal result.
The quarantine list and reconciliation counts are in memory per transport and count per call; they are not persisted for operator review or exported as telemetry yet.
No PodSource over the Kubernetes watch API exists yet; PodView in the cases relists the same fake API server.
The transport carries spawn only; command, drain, terminate and recover belong to later packages, and the swarm router does not hold a Kubernetes runtime yet.
The launch ConfigMap and credential Secret the template mounts are not created by this package.
